\cpara{Brennan's angle, ``the obvious'': why is the energy of the quantum Hamiltonian, which sets how fast the ``little arrows'' rotate, necessarily the energy that curves spacetime? It is modeled on Einstein's step, described in ``Einstein's Speed,'' that made inertial and gravitational mass ``necessarily equivalent, not just coincidentally equivalent.''}
\cpara{Yin: the question seems too obvious for Eld science to have missed.}
\cpara{Hiriwa: the answer is needed whether or not it was known.}
\cpara{Taji proposes a proof that an exception to the equality would break a conservation law.}

\cfact{Physics had a result of this kind before the story was written. In 1964 Steven Weinberg derived, from general properties of quantum scattering (the S-matrix), the ``Equality of Gravitational and Inertial Mass'' (his title): a massless spin-two particle must interact with all particles ``with equal strength,'' and the same condition also ``enforces energy-momentum conservation'' (Porrati's summary, arXiv:0804.4672). It bears on Brennan's question. It is also the kind of proof, from ``some appealing principle,'' that Hiriwa sets aside in the next line.}
\cpara{Hiriwa restates the question: not a proof from a principle, but a view in which the two energies are one and cannot be separated even in thought.}
\cpara{Brennan accepts the rephrasing.}

\cpara{The story ends as someone has an idea. It does not say whose, or what. Like ``The Ritual,'' it shows the method and the stakes and stops before any result.}
